source.notes: No official marking scheme is published with this paper; questions carry no official answer. From the CISCE Archive Library ISC 2019 question-paper bundle ISC-20191.zip (a Word-generated PDF with a real text layer). Paper code '1219-860' printed in the footer of every page. Cover: '(Maximum Marks: 100)', '(Time allowed: Three hours)', additional 15 minutes reading time, 6 printed pages. Section A (80 marks) is compulsory; candidates attempt all questions EITHER from Section B (vectors, 3-D geometry, area; 20 marks) OR Section C (commerce/economics applications, regression, linear programming; 20 marks). Both Sections B and C are included, so the pack's marks total (120 counting one alternative per OR pair) exceeds maxMarks (100) by design. Question 1 is printed '[10×2]' and Questions 15 and 19 '[3×2]'; each sub-part is its own entry. OR choices (Q3, 5, 8, 12, 14, 16, 17, 20, 21) share a choiceGroup equal to the question number; alternatives labelled (a)/(b) as printed. Notation: the paper uses MathType/Equation Editor objects; in the text layer minus signs, fraction bars, integral and summation signs, modulus bars, vector arrows, bars over means and integral limits are lost or scrambled, and powers are flattened. These were rebuilt inline from pypdfium2 page renders (flagged, confidence MEDIUM). Math-italic letters are normalised to plain letters. Q1(viii) (L'Hospital's rule) is mapped to continuity-differentiability-and-differentiation. The break-even item Q19(a) and the regression items Q19(c) and Q20 have no matching chapter slug and are left with chapter null. No cognitive-level tags are printed on this paper.

questions.text:
A carpenter has 90, 80 and 50 running feet respectively of teak wood, plywood and rosewood which is used to produce product A and product B. Each unit of product A requires 2, 1 and 1 running feet and each unit of product B requires 1, 2 and 1 running feet of teak wood, plywood and rosewood respectively. If product A is sold for ₹ 48 per unit and product B is sold for ₹ 40 per unit, how many units of product A and product B should be produced and sold by the carpenter, in order to obtain the maximum gross income?
Formulate the above as a Linear Programming Problem and solve it, indicating clearly the feasible region in the graph.
